articles.title: Many FTA benefits untapped: RBI
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Indian exporters are leaving much of the benefit of the country’s expanding free-trade network untapped, with only 20-30% of eligible shipments
articles.body: MUMBAI: Indian exporters are leaving much of the benefit of the country’s expanding free-trade network untapped, with only 20-30% of eligible shipments using preferential tariffs against 60-70% in partner countries, RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said. As a result, 70-80% of eligible Indian exports continue to enter partner markets under regular most-favoured-nation (MFN) tariffs, making them less competitive than goods from countries that use trade agreements more effectively.India has trade agreements with UAE, Australia, EFTA, Oman, UK, Asean, Japan and South Korea, offering lower or zero import duties on eligible goods. Yet exporters, particularly smaller firms, have failed to fully claim these benefits. “It is an opportunity we are leaving on the table,” he said.Speaking at the SME Finance & Investment Summit here on Friday, Malhotra urged MSMEs to break out of a low-growth trap by investing in technology, raising productivity, formalising operations and expanding overseas. He outlined a five-point action plan for businesses and called on lenders to combine digital data with relationship-based banking to widen access to credit.The challenge begins with scale. About 99% of Indian MSMEs remain micro-enterprises, with few graduating into large businesses. The transition rate is far below that in Australia (44%), Israel (42%), Indonesia (31%) and Poland (30%). “By one estimate, only about 10% of India’s large companies in 2022 had been MSMEs at any point after 2000... Too many of our firms are born small and stay small,” Malhotra said.One deterrent has been the fear of losing regulatory concessions and subsidies upon crossing the thresholds for MSME classification. Govt has raised these limits to reduce that disincentive. But size is only part of the problem. Value added per worker in Indian MSMEs is just 26% of the level in large domestic enterprises, leaving them behind both advanced economies and emerging-market peers such as Brazil and Mexico. Raising productivity to the global top-quartile level could add 11% to India’s GDP.Technology adoption is another weakness. AI penetration among Indian MSMEs is estimated at 15%, below China, the US and Germany. Although 76% of MSME leaders use AI in some form, only 5% have embedded it in core operations. Informality compounds the problem: inadequate bookkeeping, delayed tax filings and cash transactions leave lenders with little reliable information on business cash flows, forcing them to depend on physical collateral.Money habits form by age 7. articles.summary: MUMBAI: A day after sensex hit a 10-month high, profit-taking in banking stocks and RIL, which had led the recent rally, pulled the index down 989 points
articles.body: MUMBAI: A day after sensex hit a 10-month high, profit-taking in banking stocks and RIL, which had led the recent rally, pulled the index down 989 points to 83,339. On NSE, Nifty lost 277 points to close at 25,607.The day’s correction in the stock market came on the back of strong selling by domestic funds while net buying by foreign funds showed signs of slowing. At close of session, domestic institutional investors were net sellers at Rs 556 crore while foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) were net buyers at Rs 1,634 crore, data on BSE website showed.The day’s slide left investors poorer by nearly Rs 1 lakh crore with the aggregate market capitalisation of all the companies listed on the BSE at Rs 513.1 lakh crore, exchange data showed.Silver hits 6% circuit on MCXSilver prices on MCX hit the 6% upper circuit in early trade on Friday after gaining more than 10% in international markets. Silver futures for Dec delivery touched an intraday high of Rs 1.55 lakh per kg before easing to around Rs 1.53 lakh in late trade. Analysts attributed international gains mainly to short covering and said there were insufficient reasons to expect a prolonged rally in silver. Domestic gold prices also rose more than 3% to about Rs 1.27 lakh per 10 grams, tracking similar international gains.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.body: JAIPUR/NEW DELHI: In his first comments since the US Trade Representative announced its move to levy up to 25% additional tariffs on Indian exports, commerce minister Piyush Goyal Friday said the trade deal with the US is close to culmination.“The process and pathway, which was always something, which held back finalising the deal, is now taking some shape,” he said at an event. While talks have been underway for 20 months, India’s trade ties have come under repeated pressure due to Trump’s tariff policy, dotted with flip-flops and with no consistency. Govt has been trudging with caution, seeking to ensure that the country’s interests are protected, without annoying the Trump administration, which had slapped 50% additional tariffs on Indian exports.“Our talks with the US are continuing. The US is our largest trade partner with exports of over $90 billion. It is an important market. We should be holding discussions with them and we should prepare for an FTA that offers a mutually win-win solution,” commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal told reporters in Jaipur without offering any timeline for finalising a trade deal.The US has proposed 25% additional tariffs following two section 301 investigations, and offered to lower it to 17% in case India signed a trade deal. In the past Goyal and Agrawal have has stated on multiple occasions that the groundwork for a trade deal has been done and it can be signed once the US tariff framework is in place, provided India gets a comparative advantage over its rivals such as China, Bangladesh, Vietnam, Sri Lanka and Pakistan.Asked if the proposed tariffs on India were unfair, Agrawal said: “They have their own tariff policy and I would not like to discuss that. Section 301 is an instrument available with them, which has in the past also been used to investigate and levy tariffs. Now they have conducted investigation against 16 countries and given a draft notification. We are examining it and we will file our response. The final notification will come after hearing us.”Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: Retailers pitch big buys on Black Friday
articles.summary: BENGALURU/DELHI: Indian retailers are using Black Friday to draw shoppers back between Diwali and the year-end sales.
articles.body: BENGALURU/DELHI: Indian retailers are using Black Friday to draw shoppers back between Diwali and the year-end sales. Once largely online, the sale now extends to malls and electronics stores, with offers ranging from designer handbags to appliance bundles costing nearly Rs 1.5 lakh.Early sales at Nexus Select Malls point to growth in the low teens in fashion, beauty and accessories, said Nishank Joshi, its chief marketing officer. Electronics sales were growing steadily, though it was too early to tell whether shoppers were spending more per visit than last year.DLF Retail expects its malls to draw double-digit growth in footfalls over a regular weekend, said Pushpa Bector, its group executive director and business head. She estimated a 15-20% increase in sales across its retail partners.In Delhi, Vijay Sales advertised appliance packages from Rs 49,990 to Rs 1,49,990. The cheapest included a TV, fridge and washing machine. Reliance Digital advertised the iPhone 17 Pro from Rs 54,990 after an in-store discount, a handset trade-in, an exchange bonus and cashback.Croma advertised Samsung’s Galaxy S26 Ultra at Rs 85,999, including the exchange value of a Galaxy S25 Ultra. Lifestyle advertised discounts of up to 50% from Nov 25 to 29.“We see the biggest opportunity in premium electronics, appliances, furniture and luxury, where consumers often decide what to buy well ahead and wait for a good deal,” said Anand Ramanathan, partner and consumer industry leader at Deloitte South Asia.In Deloitte’s March 2026 survey, 65% of Indian respondents were willing to make a large non-essential purchase, down five percentage points from February. Only 43% felt they could afford the things that brought them joy.Tata CLiQ’s sale began on Nov 19. CEO Gopal Asthana said daily business had doubled compared with regular days and he expected it to exceed three times the usual level over the weekend. He expects 30% growth over last year’s Black Friday at Tata CLiQ Luxury, where watches, apparel and footwear were most popular.Coach’s India site listed its Brooklyn Shoulder Bag 39 at Rs 37,500 against a reference price of Rs 62,500. Charles & Keith offered up to 40% off selected handbags and shoes. Tom Ford Beauty and Bobbi Brown placed less emphasis on the event, an industry expert said.At handbag brand Miraggio, two days of a buy-one-get-one offer on its website generated about twice the sales and more than 2.5 times the orders of last year’s 10-day buy-two-get-one promotion, said founder and CEO Mohit Jain. On marketplaces, its average order value rose 2-5% from last year.Around 30% of styles sold during the event come from new collections, a Myntra spokesperson said, citing demand for winter clothing and wedding wear. GoKwik’s network recorded 5.8 lakh online orders worth Rs 90 crore by 8.53 pm on Friday, averaging Rs 1,551 per order.“The weeks that follow give us a better read on how much demand the weekend added and how much it brought forward,” Joshi said.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Federal regulators shut $6 billion Indiana lender in biggest bank failure in over two years
articles.summary: Federal regulators shut down Indiana-based United Fidelity on Friday night, marking the biggest US bank failure since April 2024.
articles.body: Federal regulators shut down Indiana-based United Fidelity on Friday night, marking the biggest US bank failure since April 2024. The Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. announced that First Citizens has agreed to assume all of United Fidelity’s deposits and assets. FDIC officials say customers with deposits at United Fidelity will “retain all of their funds” as well as their deposit insurance coverage, now as customers of First Citizens, which also served as a distressed buyer in the larger Silicon Valley Bank failure of 2023. Officials stressed that Friday evening and over the weekend, United Fidelity depositors can still access their funds, including by writing checks, visiting ATMs and using their debit cards. In a sign of how distressed United Fidelity was when regulators decided to step in, the FDIC estimates the failure will wipe out $1.83 billion of the industry’s deposit insurance fund. That represents an unusually high 31% loss on United Fidelity’s $5.9 billion in total assets as of the end of September. In another likely sign of United Fidelity’s troubled state, First Citizens said it has only agreed to assume $4.5 billion of the bank’s deposits. That is well shy of the $5.4 billion the FDIC said United Fidelity held as of the end of September. The FDIC said the deposit accounts that transfer to First Citizens exclude “certain brokered deposits” but did not disclose how many or why. “We believe this transaction is both financially and strategically compelling,” First Citizens CEO Frank Holding Jr. said in a statement, “and we look forward to welcoming our new customers, earning their trust and positioning our company for continued success.” First Citizens agreed to take on $3.1 billion of loans held by United Fidelity — but only at a steep discount. First Citizens said its winning bid included a deep asset discount of $2.6 billion, suggesting the lender is concerned the loans are troubled. United Fidelity’s 22 branches across Indiana, Illinois, Florida, Colorado and the US Virgin Islands will reopen as First Citizens branches starting on Saturday, according to the FDIC. It’s the biggest US bank failure since Philadelphia-based Republic Bank closed in April 2024 with $6 billion in assets, according to FDIC data. United Fidelity becomes the second-biggest bank failure since the 2023 regional banking crisis that included the implosions of both Silicon Valley Bank and First Republic. Fearing other banks would go under next, US officials eventually stepped in with a rescue that helped prevent further failures.
